1.point: The verse and the Imam's 'one year is enough' set the road's measure as time, and the epilogue will lay the chapters' small steps on three rungs: a week, a month, a year.
steps: Open with the verse's fifth mark and the Imam's answer that a year is enough
Say that the chapter arranges the chapters' Try-this steps on three rungs and hand off to the rules

2.point: A beginner starts inside the law with one act that fits him, small enough to keep and grown gradually; he does not wait for a guide, but tests any he follows.
steps: Every step stands on the obligations already kept
The act is chosen to suit the person
It is small, measured by ourselves and not by the Prophet or the Imams
It grows gradually; rushing is the opposite error
The road is not closed for want of a guide; the first steps need only a teacher of practices
Any teacher found is tested by the law, long company and where he turns people

3.point: The first week is repentance once, then one daily act of a few minutes fixed to the time of day when the heart is already most present.
steps: Start with the prayer of repentance, once
Choose one act and fix it to the time of day where the heart is most present
Lay out the chapters' steps by time of day so the reader can pick one

4.point: The month keeps the same single act daily, adding nothing; if Shaʿban, Ramadan or Dhu'l-Qaʿdah falls in it, the act lengthens, but only within the traveller's capacity.
steps: Keep the act daily, add nothing
Shaʿban lengthens the petitions into the whole Munajat
Ramadan lengthens the Qur'an reading
Dhu'l-Qaʿdah brings the prayer of repentance back
The heavy programmes for these months are a ceiling governed by the opening rules

5.point: Keep one practice for a year, do not stop when the year ends, and ask God for the constancy itself, as the Munajat does.
steps: A year is the teachers' measure for one practice
Name what the year's practice can be
The year is kept in hope of what the Sheikh says it brings
The year is not a finish line; stopping slips back
What matters is acceptance by God, not the deed's size
The keeping itself is asked of God in the Munajat's words

¶1.why: Hook: the verse's fifth mark and the Imam's 'one year is enough' set up the time-measure the whole epilogue uses.

¶3.why: Supplies step 1: every step stands on the obligations; recommended acts build on them.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Supplies step 4: the opposite error, rushing, and the elder's call for gradual improvement.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Supplies step 6: how any teacher found is tested.

¶12.label: advance

¶13.label: advance

¶14.label: advance

¶16.label: support

¶21.label: advance

¶22.label: advance

¶23.label: advance

¶24.label: advance

¶27.label: advance

¶32.why: Supplies the last step: the Munajat's request for constancy, with the keeping placed in God's hands. The two sentences placing the petition relative to Part Five's opening and Chapter Six's start are location notes the step does not need.
